previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, COPD, type 2 diabetes, and polysubstance use was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and new-onset chest pain. He had not taken his heart failure medications for several days and presented with signs of fluid overload. Initial evaluation revealed elevated cardiac biomarkers and EKG changes concerning for ischemia, though no acute myocardial infarction occurred. He was treated for acute on chronic systolic heart failure with IV furosemide, later transitioned to oral torsemide 40mg daily. An echocardiogram showed worsening left ventricular function. A chest CTA revealed a growing spiculated lung nodule suspicious for cancer and stable mediastinal lymphadenopathy. A bronchoscopy and lymph node biopsy were performed, but the lung nodule could not be sampled due to hemodynamic instability. The lymph node fluid showed no infection or malignancy on initial testing. His diabetes was difficult to control, requiring insulin adjustment. He was discharged home with close follow-up for the lung nodule, substance use counseling through a dual diagnosis program, and medication management.
